claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a narrow aggregate-readiness basis despite a known small-business onboarding segment gap, relying on aggregate pass results, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general public AI governance guidance.
specific_concerns: The admissible record contains a named segment evaluation gap for small-business onboarding that misses target by 1.3 percentage points.
That affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which makes materiality harder to dismiss under the stated policy text.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The policy text says materiality is not resolved by labels like non-core or low-volume when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
The packet argues aggregate readiness and ongoing monitoring, but that does not show the required disclosure was made or that approved risk acceptance exists before launch.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record merely because aggregate readiness clears threshold and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents.
That public governance principles and model-card guidance are sufficient support for certification under the specific internal materiality policy at issue.
Any implied claim that the disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement has been satisfied; no such evidence appears in the provided record.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether the small-business onboarding gap requires disclosure before launch.
Provide the actual launch disclosure or model-card language showing the material limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide approved risk-acceptance documentation if the team intends to launch before remediation.
Provide evidence that the named paid pilot commitments were amended, deferred, or otherwise no longer in scope.
Provide updated segment-specific evaluation results showing the small-business onboarding gap is resolved.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
If disclosure of a material limitation is required, launch certification needs evidence that the issue was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public guidance may support general governance framing, but it does not override the specific policy predicate in the case record.
